READING_COMPREHENSION.readingText: In the UK, most secondary school students wear a uniform every day. A typical uniform consists of a white shirt, a striped tie, a dark jumper, and grey trousers or a skirt. In Australia, students also wear wide hats to protect their skin from the strong sun. In many other countries, like Spain or the United States, students in state schools do not wear a uniform. They usually wear comfortable everyday clothes like T-shirts, hoodies, and jeans. Many students like uniforms because they don't have to decide what to wear every morning.

Why do Australian students wear wide hats?
Do students in state schools in Spain usually wear a uniform?
What is one reason students like uniforms?
questions.a: They don't have to choose clothes each morning
options: They don't have to choose clothes each morning

READING_COMPREHENSION.category: What Are They Doing Right Now?
READING_COMPREHENSION.readingText: It is ten past eleven on a sunny Tuesday morning at Greenhill School. Right now, Class 2B is having a break in the school courtyard. Marco and Diego are playing football near the goalposts. Sophie is sitting on a wooden bench and reading a comic book. Mr Anderson, the history teacher, is drinking coffee in the staffroom. Some students are standing in line at the canteen because they are buying fresh sandwiches and apples. Nobody is sleeping!

questions.q: What is Class 2B doing right now?
questions.a: Having a break in the courtyard
options: Having a break in the courtyard

questions.q: What are Marco and Diego doing?

READING_COMPREHENSION.category: SDG - Give Your Clothes a Second Life
READING_COMPREHENSION.readingText: Did you know that producing one single cotton T-shirt takes about 2,700 litres of water? Fast fashion creates millions of tonnes of waste each year when people throw old clothes in the rubbish bin. Today, our school eco-club is organising a clothes swap event. Students bring clean clothes that they no longer wear and trade them for other clothes. If clothes have holes, members learn how to sew and repair them. Small actions like this protect rivers, reduce pollution, and help families save money.

What is the school eco-club organising?
What do students do with clothes that have holes?

options: They learn to sew and repair them
They throw them in the river

questions.a: It reduces pollution and saves money
options: It reduces pollution and saves money
